summary: Two target blocks must cross the same transfer bottleneck, increasing synchronization pressure and handoff competition.
Two chefs clean and cook two items through a one-slot pass table, creating reusable handoff structure with limited shared resources.
Extends the kitchen pipeline to three items, increasing long-horizon causal chaining and pass/stove contention.
A one-slot sink, stove, and pass table create a small but order-sensitive scheduling problem with shared buffers.
Three items and single-capacity shared resources produce many near-equivalent prefixes but few good global orderings.
Adds one more disconnected objective and keeps a sparse relay topology, increasing both allocation ambiguity and synchronization load.
